summary: Ustaz Azlan shares his experience at an Asia-Pacific conference for new Muslims in Singapore, which reminded him that the whole sirah is the story of converts and the grief they carry when family do not follow. He then covers the bad and good effects of the Shi'b Abi Talib boycott, the last visit of 25 Quraysh leaders to the ailing Abu Talib, the Prophet's offer of a single word, and his final plea to his uncle. Abu Talib died without saying the shahadah; the ustaz mentions the Prophet's reaction, At-Tawbah 113 and Al-Qasas 56, Ali's handling of the burial, Al-Abbas's question, and Abu Bakr's words when his father Abu Quhafah became Muslim. The class closes with Q&A on the challenges of new Muslims and a reminder about jahiliyyah and our duty to be a lamp.
keyPoints: The whole sirah is the story of converts, and many new Muslims grieve when close family do not follow.
The boycott left bad effects: unrecorded deaths, declining health, ruined economy and hindered da'wah, yet Makkan society began to sympathise.
Twenty-five Quraysh leaders visited Abu Talib with a 'ceasefire' offer; the Prophet SAW answered with an offer of one word, La ilaha illallah.
The Prophet SAW pleaded with Abu Talib at the end, but he died on the religion of Abdul Muttalib without saying the shahadah.
The Prophet SAW swore to keep seeking forgiveness for Abu Talib until forbidden; At-Tawbah 113 came down, and Al-Qasas 56 states that guidance is Allah's.
Abu Bakr said he would rather Abu Talib had become Muslim than his own father, as it would please the Prophet's heart more.
We need empathy and layered understanding with new Muslims, and must be a lamp, not a reason people turn from Islam.

lessons.title: Cherish being born into Islam
lessons.body: We who were born Muslim hardly appreciate how much we have.

lessons.title: Do not pressure new Muslims
lessons.body: Our excitement can become heavy pressure on someone just starting.

lessons.title: Live the sirah, do not just read it
lessons.body: The sirah is understood by listening to scholars and mixing with people who go through these emotions.

lessons.title: Do not only hand down rulings
lessons.body: New Muslims are frustrated by religious people who only judge in black and white.

lessons.title: Suffering has a long tail
lessons.body: The period of hardship seems short but its effects are very long.

lessons.title: Know the person's soft spot
lessons.body: Da'wah requires studying a person's soft spot, as the Prophet SAW offered power to the Quraysh leaders.

lessons.title: Faith is submission
lessons.body: Abu Talib knew the truth but did not submit; Islam means submission.

lessons.title: Guidance belongs to Allah
lessons.body: Even the Prophet SAW, who loved Abu Talib dearly, could not give him guidance.

lessons.title: Show empathy to the bereaved
lessons.body: Do not pass verdicts on a convert's parents who did not say the shahadah; console with empathy.

lessons.title: Honour non-Muslim funerals
lessons.body: Where no polytheistic ritual is involved, we may attend and pay last respects.

lessons.title: Do not seek forgiveness for one who died clearly without the shahadah
lessons.body: We may grieve and weep, but not ask forgiveness for them.

lessons.title: Be careful and layered
lessons.body: Converts' situations are complex, including old habits like alcohol, so we need to be more humane.

lessons.title: Our religion is solid
lessons.body: Islam demands total change and has a firm belief system.

lessons.title: Know jahiliyyah to appreciate Islam
lessons.body: Umar feared a generation that never saw jahiliyyah.

lessons.title: Do not be why people turn from Islam
lessons.body: Our words and conduct can keep people from seeing Islam's beauty.

glossary.meaning: A person newly embracing Islam; the ustaz says we are all 'new' in understanding Islam.
The place in Makkah where the Prophet SAW taught new companions; also the name of an association in Singapore.
The year covering the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah and the Ta'if event.
A person's weak point or what occupies his mind most, used as a door for da'wah.
Surrender; the root sense of Islam as full submission to Allah.
The way of life and culture opposed to Islam, including racism and tribalism.
The moment the soul is taken; Satan uses maximum tactics to mislead then.
The word of tawhid; what matters is that it is lived and understood, not just said.

dalil.context: Quraysh were amazed that the gods were made one; the ustaz reads the relevant part of Sad verses 1-7.
dalil.translation: How can he claim that all the gods are but one God? What an astonishing thing [to claim]!’

dalil.context: The Sahih Bukhari chapter on the death of Abu Talib; Abu Jahal reminded him of the religion of Abdul Muttalib.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said: Uncle, say one word, La ilaha illallah, and I will plead for you with Allah.

dalil.context: Said when Abu Talib died without the shahadah, before At-Tawbah 113.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said: I will keep asking forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Ali never felt happier than on the day he heard that supplication.
dalil.translation: Ali told the Prophet SAW that his misguided uncle had died; the Prophet SAW told him to see to him and bury him, then prayed for Ali.

dalil.context: The ustaz calls it the Prophet's intercession; another Muslim hadith describes the lightest punishment.
dalil.translation: Al-Abbas asked whether the Prophet SAW benefited Abu Talib, who used to defend him; he answered yes, he is in the lowest level of Hell, in shoes of fire that boil his brain.

dalil.context: Mentioned in Ar-Rahiq Al-Makhtum and other books, but the ustaz says it is weak.
dalil.translation: Al-Abbas said he saw Abu Talib saying La ilaha illallah; the Prophet SAW replied that he did not hear it.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi call it sahih.
dalil.translation: Abu Bakr brought his father Abu Quhafah to the Prophet SAW, who stroked his head and invited him to Islam, and he said the shahadah. Abu Bakr wept, saying he would rather it had been Abu Talib so the Prophet's heart would be eased.

dalil.context: Mentioned when explaining the weight of this word.
dalil.translation: Whoever says La ilaha illallah enters Paradise; whoever's last words are La ilaha illallah enters Paradise.

dalil.context: It is not for the Prophet and the believers to ask forgiveness for polytheists, even if close relatives.
dalil.translation: It is not fitting for the Prophet and the believers to ask forgiveness for the idolaters- even if they are related to them- after having been shown that they are the inhabitants of the Blaze:

dalil.context: You cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.
dalil.translation: You [Prophet] cannot guide everyone you love to the truth; it is God who guides whoever He will: He knows best those who will follow guidance.
